records.name: Integer Division: Truncation Towards Zero vs Floor Towards Negative Infinity

interpretation.python_behavior: Integer division (//) floors toward negative infinity (e.g., 7 // 2 = 3; -7 // 2 = -4).
interpretation.javascript_behavior: Division (/) always performs floating-point division (e.g., 7 / 2 = 3.5; -7 / 2 = -3.5). Math.trunc(a / b) emulates C++; Math.floor(a / b) emulates Python.
interpretation.sql_behavior: In SQL Server / PostgreSQL, integer / integer performs integer division with truncation toward zero. In Oracle / Snowflake, division yields exact decimal/float.

risks: Migrating C++ or SQL integer division of negative numbers to Python // results in silent off-by-one errors (-3 vs -4)
validation_rules: To preserve C++ truncation toward zero in Python, use: int(a / b) or math.trunc(a / b) instead of a // b

records.name: Modulo Operator Sign Semantics (% Operator)

interpretation.cpp_java_js_behavior: Sign of result matches dividend (a): -7 % 2 = -1; 7 % -2 = 1 (remainder operation).
interpretation.mathematical_distinction: Python computes mathematical modulo (a - b * floor(a / b)). C++/Java/JS compute remainder (a - b * trunc(a / b)).

risks: Negative indexing or cyclic array indexing (-1 % N) yields negative index in C++/JS but positive index in Python
validation_rules: When translating Python a % b to JS: use ((a % b) + b) % b to preserve Python positive modulo

records.name: Signed Integer Arithmetic Overflow Handling

interpretation.cpp_behavior: Signed integer overflow is Undefined Behavior (UB); compilers may optimize away safety checks.
interpretation.java_csharp_behavior: Wraps modulo 2^32 or 2^64 using 2's complement representation without throwing exception (unless 'checked' block in C#).
interpretation.python_behavior: Transparently promotes to arbitrary precision integer; overflow impossible for pure integers.
interpretation.javascript_behavior: Silently transitions into loss-of-precision floats above 2^53 - 1.

risks: Algorithms relying on 32-bit integer overflow wrapping (e.g. hash codes) fail in Python because integers grow unboundedly
validation_rules: In Python, emulate 32-bit wrap explicitly: (result & 0xFFFFFFFF) or ctypes.c_int32(result).value
